factsAccepted: The current mid-market ICP is saturating: a third-party estimate indicates ~78% of target accounts already have a CSPM solution, and MQL volume in this segment is down 20% YoY. Three large platform vendors now bundle CSPM into broader suites, shifting buyer preference toward consolidation. The pool of un-penetrated, in-budget demand in the current ICP is shrinking.

New-logo bookings are flat YoY despite a 35% larger sales team, the sales cycle extended from 95 to 165 days, and win rate fell from 28% to 18%. Top-of-funnel lead-to-opportunity conversion is down 30%. Adding capacity produced no incremental output, indicating the constraint is upstream demand, not rep productivity per se.

Recent losses are increasingly attributed to 'platform consolidation' (62% of losses) rather than head-to-head feature comparison (21%). Buyers are not rejecting the product on capability; they are choosing to consolidate cloud security into broader platforms they already own. This is a demand/budget-allocation shift, not a feature gap.

Retention is excellent and stable: NRR 116%, gross retention 97%. Existing customers value and expand on the product, which contradicts a product-quality or differentiation-collapse explanation for the new-logo stall. The problem is in finding new in-budget demand, not in the product's value to those who buy it.

Gross margin is healthy at 79% and runway is 30 months, so the business is not in an economics crisis; however, CAC per new logo has risen sharply because a larger team is closing the same number of deals over longer cycles, which is the efficiency symptom the board is watching.
